
## Terms
* A genome is the complete set of genetic material (DNA or RNA) in an organism.
* The transcriptome is the full set of RNA transcripts produced by the genome.
* The methylome is the complete profile of DNA methylation modifications across the genome.
* The epigenome comprises all chemical modifications to DNA and histone proteins that regulate gene expression without altering the underlying DNA sequence.
* The mCpG epigenome specifically maps methylated cytosine-guanine (CpG) dinucleotide sites that typically repress gene activity.
* The chromatin epigenome details how DNA is packaged and structurally wrapped around histones into accessible or closed states.
* The proteome is the complete set of proteins expressed by an organism's genome.
